briefs.title: Sunday Deep Dive: Eisenkot Gets the Mandate, a Leaked Russian Death Toll, and Iraq's Lights Go Out
briefs.bluf: The week's real shift was political, not military: US voters punished the Iran war, oil fell about 13% as traders priced in pressure for a deal, and on November 8 Trump told CNN new strikes are highly unlikely if Iran signs a strong agreement, even as minor US strikes continued. In Israel, Herzog handed Gadi Eisenkot the mandate three days early, but his road to a government runs through Avigdor Lieberman's veto on the Arab parties, which now hold a record 19 seats. Russia and Ukraine meet in Abu Dhabi on November 10 to 11 with heavier delegations on both sides, as hackers released what they say are Rosstat records showing up to 450,000 Russian war deaths. Below the headlines: a drone strike shut Kurdistan's Khor Mor gas field as winter starts, Paraguay's bank collapse froze about $380 million of pension money, and Taiwan detained a pro Beijing party founder three weeks before its local elections. Mississippi's Senate race is still uncalled, with Colom ahead by 2,574 votes per AP.
briefs._s: sunday deep dive: eisenkot gets the mandate, a leaked russian death toll, and iraq's lights go out the week's real shift was political, not military: us voters punished the iran war, oil fell about 13% as traders priced in pressure for a deal, and on november 8 trump told cnn new strikes are highly unlikely if iran signs a strong agreement, even as minor us strikes continued. in israel, herzog handed gadi eisenkot the mandate three days early, but his road to a government runs through avigdor lieberman's veto on the arab parties, which now hold a record 19 seats. russia and ukraine meet in abu dhabi on november 10 to 11 with heavier delegations on both sides, as hackers released what they say are rosstat records showing up to 450,000 russian war deaths. below the headlines: a drone strike shut kurdistan's khor mor gas field as winter starts, paraguay's bank collapse froze about $380 million of pension money, and taiwan detained a pro beijing party founder three weeks before its local elections. mississippi's senate race is still uncalled, with colom ahead by 2,574 votes per ap. house democrats move toward impeaching hegseth as a fired admiral flips nancy mace's seat yahoo news' running midterm coverage on november 8 reported the house could vote this week on impeaching defense secretary pete hegseth, and that a navy admiral hegseth had fired won nancy mace's former south carolina house seat. details of the articles of impeachment were not collected this run. mississippi's affidavit ballot pileup traces back to a state roll cleanup that used experian credit data scripps reported that thousands of mississippians who showed up on november 3 found themselves marked inactive and had to cast affidavit (provisional) ballots, the main reason the hyde-smith and colom race is still uncounted. the state had used experian consumer address data to maintain its voter rolls; one voter said a clerk told him experian placed him in another city although he has not moved in a decade. experian says it has not served the state since 2025 and that its product supplied supplemental addresses and was never meant to validate voter records. the secretary of state's office did not answer scripps; npr separately reported that secretary michael watson's office could not say how many affidavit ballots remain, with over 9,000 processed by midday november 6. hyde-smith asks all 82 mississippi counties to set aside affidavit ballots; colom calls it unlawful hyde-smith's legal team wrote every county election commission asking that affidavit ballots be kept apart and each one's handling documented, citing state law on post election ballot handling. state gop chairman mike hurst called it a standard preservation step in a close race. colom's lawyers replied that state law has no provision for segregating counted affidavit ballots and that the demand threatens ballot secrecy. as of saturday afternoon ap had colom ahead by 2,574 votes, 49.1% to 48.8%, with about 97% counted; his lead has grown with each batch since election night. hyde-smith's campaign says thousands of votes remain in republican counties. alaska: a second 'dan sullivan' on the ballot drew about 3,600 votes in a race peltola leads by 637 with about a quarter of ballots still out, mary peltola led senator dan sullivan 48.02% to 47.72% as of november 4 afternoon, a 637 vote gap, with ranked choice tabulation starting november 18. a petersburg man also named dan j. sullivan drew roughly 3,600 votes. the sullivan campaign, citing a new york times report, says democratic operatives helped put him on the ballot and calls it the biggest cheating scandal in state history; the peltola campaign denies it. per just security's tracker, doj appealed the november 1 dismissal of its alaska certification suit to the ninth circuit the same day. incoming homeland security chair orders dhs to preserve every record as oversight democrats tell miller to 'lawyer up' representative bennie thompson, expected to chair house homeland security in january, wrote dhs secretary markwayne mullin demanding preservation of all records, emails and contracts. after trump named stephen miller chief of staff, representative robert garcia, the likely oversight chair, said democrats will keep investigating miller's conduct, with ice use of force, including the killings of alex pretti and renee good earlier this year, named as a top priority. hakeem jeffries said miller should be fired; mullin's public answer was that deportations will continue. free beacon: maine's new democratic senator troy jackson backed bills for clients of a firm where his son lobbied the washington free beacon reported that troy jackson's son chace joined a lobbying firm founded by jackson's former chief of staff in 2022, and that jackson, then a maine senate leader, introduced bills benefiting that firm's corporate clients, including one that would have let a lender avoid the state's interest rate caps. the son stopped lobbying when jackson left the state senate. the piece names neither the firm nor the bills and carries no response from jackson. hormuz traffic slowed but did not collapse under the october attack wave; old shadow fleet tankers are being pulled into legal gulf trades lloyd's list intelligence, the shipping data arm of the london trade paper, counted 116 non iranian cargo transits in the week of october 19 to 25, against 124 the week before, with the fall almost entirely in ships leaving the gulf while inbound traffic stayed near normal. ukmto, the british naval office that logs incidents, has recorded 144 events since the war began, and ships kept sailing in about three quarters of them. more than 50 tankers and gas carriers that were not under sanctions have shifted into gulf trades, and tonnage that once served iran, russia and venezuela is now being drawn into gulf exports. the brief is moving to a fortnightly schedule, next due november 19. russia agreed to give iran 90 helicopter mounted missile launchers, the financial times reports iran international, the london based persian language channel critical of tehran, relayed a financial times report that moscow agreed to supply 90 launchers for precision guided missiles that mount on helicopters. the same missiles are in wide use by russian forces in ukraine. neither the launcher model, the helicopter platform, delivery dates nor payment terms were given in the relayed text, and no iranian official response was reported. belgium's defense minister says tehran warned of 'dire consequences' if reza pahlavi spoke in brussels belgium's defense minister said on november 6 that iran warned his government of serious consequences if it allowed reza pahlavi, the exiled son of the last shah, to speak in brussels. the event went ahead. the minister also said the war between the us and iran affects belgian economic and security interests. iran international gave no detail on how the warning was delivered. tehran court sentences a social media activist to death over posts on x as executions pass 690 for the year a tehran court sentenced amirhossein mousavi, a social media activist, to death over his posts on x, according to his lawyer. separately, iran human rights, an oslo based monitor, counted at least 77 executions in october and 691 so far in 2026. these sit alongside the protester death sentences already reported from mashhad and isfahan. saudi led coalition says houthis tried to hit riyadh; the houthis now count 4,460 saudi strikes since the latest escalation on november 8 the coalition spokesman, turki al-maliki, said two ballistic missile launchers were destroyed in saada after an attempted houthi attack on riyadh, and that five missiles aimed at saudi territory were intercepted since dawn. houthi spokesman yahya saree claimed 91 saudi air and missile strikes in 24 hours across six provinces and a cumulative 4,460 since the latest round began. government forces claimed about 267 houthi fighters killed, wounded or fled on fronts from marib to taiz. nearly all figures come from the warring parties and are unverified. israeli press: an israeli strike on iran is still possible, but no major us buildup has been detected iran international relayed a ynet report, from israel's most read news site, that the israeli military is waiting on washington's next move and that a strike on iran remains an option. the same report said no significant new american military buildup had been seen. it came as trump weighed escalation against settlement after the midterm losses. herzog hands gadi eisenkot the mandate three days early; netanyahu answers with a 'national unity' pitch that keeps ben gvir president isaac herzog tasked gadi eisenkot, the former army chief who leads the centrist yashar party, with forming a government on sunday november 8, ahead of the november 11 deadline, after 67 of 120 lawmakers recommended him against 46 for netanyahu. eisenkot has 28 days, extendable by 14, and said he will not swear in a government this week even if a deal comes sooner. his initial plan is a four party minority government backed from outside by the arab list ra'am and possibly united torah judaism. netanyahu called for national unity rather than what he termed national suicide, while keeping itamar ben gvir's jewish power in the package, which yashar rejects. arab lists hold an unprecedented 19 seats, and lieberman's veto over them is now the main obstacle to ending the netanyahu era ra'am and the joint list, the two arab majority slates, won 19 seats in the october 27 election and both recommended eisenkot. avigdor lieberman of yisrael beytenu, a member of eisenkot's own bloc, refuses any government that leans on their support, citing their refusal to explicitly label hamas a terror group, although both have condemned the october 7 attack. lieberman says the only options are a 61 seat government including haredi parties or a new election. lieberman, the loudest critic of haredi draft exemptions, is reportedly negotiating with utj and shas and may bend on conscription shafaq news reports that lieberman is in talks with united torah judaism and shas, the two ultra orthodox parties, and may compromise on military conscription of yeshiva students to build a 61 seat majority without the arab lists. utj, with seven seats, declined for the first time in six elections to recommend netanyahu but also refused to back eisenkot. utj lawmaker isaac pindrus said the immediate priority is settling the status of torah students. drone strike halts all output at kurdistan's khor mor gas field, cutting up to 2,800 megawatts of power unidentified drones hit a sensitive section of the khor mor field in sulaymaniyah province on november 8, and a source told shafaq news that production and exports stopped completely. the kurdistan region's electricity ministry said generation would fall by 2,500 to 2,800 megawatts because several large plants run on the field's gas. prime minister ali al-zaidi ordered a joint federal and kurdish investigation, and the militia asaib ahl al-haq condemned the attack. no group has claimed it. iraq's prime minister and kataib hezbollah square off over airport leases and his brother's wealth; shia elders step in to prevent clashes al-zaidi cancelled three leases at mosul international airport held by companies tied to armed groups and reassigned them to international firms. kataib hezbollah, the most hardline iran aligned militia, denied controlling the contracts and asked iraq's integrity commission to investigate the finances of the premier's brother, hassan al-zaidi, while an allied mp filed questions on the premier's own wealth and advisers. ammar al-hakim and humam hamoudi, two senior shia leaders, began mediating with the backing of the ruling coordination framework to avoid an armed confrontation. us envoy tom barrack, in baghdad, said militia influence has no place in iraqi institutions. iraq's militia weapons deal is a numbers game: officials and factions cannot agree who signed what before a june 2027 deadline foreign minister fuad hussein said asaib ahl al-haq and kataib sayyid al-shuhada had accepted weapons controls; kataib sayyid al-shuhada called that inaccurate and said it signed only a separate sovereignty pledge. official tallies have moved from three of seven factions agreeing to five, with three said to have surrendered weapons, none named. the plan began october 1, the day after the us led coalition ended its mission, with handovers due by june 30, 2027, a date washington has not accepted as binding. kataib hezbollah says the 'islamic resistance in iraq' has halted operations inside iraq until further notice but has signed nothing. nechirvan barzani hosts an iranian delegation as baghdad weighs moving iranian kurdish opposition groups out of the kurdistan region kurdistan region president nechirvan barzani met an unnamed iranian delegation in erbil on november 8 to review a 2023 security pact under which baghdad committed to stop iranian kurdish armed opposition groups from using iraqi soil against iran. iraqi political forces are weighing a proposal to relocate those groups from the kurdistan region to a center elsewhere in iraq, which the groups reject. barzani said in october that the region warned them at the war's start they would not be allowed to attack iran. turkey agrees to start handing its bashiqa base in northern iraq to baghdad; sinjar's yazidi militia has placed its arms under state control after a meeting of the iraqi and turkish high level committee, al-zaidi's office said ankara will take steps toward a gradual handover of the bashiqa zilkan camp in nineveh, turkey's best known military base in iraq. a nineveh council security official told shafaq that turkish troops and vehicles have already partly left. the sinjar resistance units, a yazidi force long accused by ankara of pkk ties, have put their weapons under state control, and a joint committee will verify the process in sinjar. hackers claim rosstat records show up to 450,000 russian war deaths, released on the eve of abu dhabi two hacker groups, the belarusian cyberpartisans (an anti lukashenko collective) and silent crow (a pro ukrainian group), say they took death records from rosstat, russia's state statistics service. the cyberpartisans count at least 393,881 deaths explicitly tied to military operations from february 2022 to august 2026; silent crow puts it at up to 450,100 by adding non combat and unspecified deaths, rising from about 19,000 in 2022 to over 182,000 in 2025. kyiv post notes the records have not been independently verified and no methodology was published. for comparison, mediazona's named count stood at 285,881 on november 6. abu dhabi line ups set: russia adds ryabkov and military officers, kyiv sends umerov, budanov and arakhamia, paris says europe will be there david arakhamia, head of zelensky's parliamentary faction, told the kyiv independent that foreign intelligence chief rustem umerov leads ukraine's team, joined by himself, chief of staff kyrylo budanov and serhii kyslytsia. on november 7 moscow said it would add senior diplomats and military officials, including deputy foreign minister sergei ryabkov, to the delegation under vladimir medinsky. on november 8 french foreign minister jean noël barrot said europe will take part, contradicting kremlin statements that europeans are not invited; eu leaders are due to discuss representation on november 13. budanov said these talks are neither the last nor final. russia has declared 521 hotels in occupied zaporizhzhia 'ownerless'; at least 77 have changed hands a reuters review, republished by meduza, found occupation authorities declared more than 7,000 private and commercial properties in occupied zaporizhzhia region ownerless, including 521 hotels and resorts; at least 77 hotel properties have been transferred, 20 to state bodies. owners could keep title only by taking russian citizenship. hotelier denys katyukha lost his 100 room admiral hotel on the sea of azov to a state resort company within nine days and won a $5.1 million ukrainian court judgment russia ignores. peskov told reuters residents had a fair chance to register; ukraine's foreign ministry calls it state organized theft. mediazona names 350 russian conscripts killed in ukraine despite the kremlin's pledge not to use them mediazona, an independent russian outlet that tracks losses with bbc russian and volunteers through public records, published 350 names of conscripts killed in the war. it also has names of nearly 700 men who signed contracts during compulsory service, often under pressure or violence according to its reporting. officially conscripts only guard border regions, and the defense ministry promised early in the war to withdraw them all. moscow plans to let airlines keep flying unreturned western leased jets through 2028 vedomosti reports a draft government resolution from the transport ministry that would extend until the end of 2028 the 2022 regime letting russian airlines fly foreign leased planes and engines they never returned. of 515 leased aircraft at the start of the war, 407 stayed in russia and lessor claims were settled on 204 by 2025, leaving the rest in legal limbo. the ministry says the measure protects companies from 'unfriendly countries'. kremlin says out loud that armenia is de facto not taking part in the csto asked about armenia at his november 6 briefing, kremlin spokesman dmitry peskov said yerevan is in practice not participating in the work of the collective security treaty organization (csto), the moscow led military alliance of six former soviet states. he said next steps depend on discussions inside the organization. armenia froze its participation in 2024 but has not formally left. kraków mass shooting: nine dead including the gunman's family, prosecutors open a terrorism case on november 7 a 24 year old man identified as michał o. drove through kraków's historic center firing at random from his car with what appears to be an ar 15 style rifle, killing six people, among them a british man, and wounding 16 from poland, the uk, portugal, russia, germany and austria. his parents and sister were found dead at home in ostrowiec świętokrzyski. interior minister marcin kierwiński said initial findings point to very radical far right views, still being verified; the national prosecutor's office opened a terrorism investigation on november 8. notes from poland calls it the first mass public shooting of this type in a country with one of europe's lowest gun ownership rates. s&p puts a price on poland's institutional war: negative outlook, citing presidential vetoes and the tribunal standoff on november 6 s&p moved poland's outlook to negative and cut its local currency ratings from a to a minus, calling it one of the most significant fiscal deteriorations globally. the deficit was 7.3 percent of gdp in 2025, the second highest in the eu, and s&p projects net debt above 70 percent of gdp by 2029. it named presidential vetoes and constitutional court tensions as constraints. finance minister andrzej domański pointed to the vetoes; president nawrocki, who has vetoed a record number of bills, blames tusk's government for budget chaos. poland's tribunal crisis splits the rule of law camp: 'not a coup', but the method is questioned on october 30 seven parliament elected judges entered the constitutional tribunal escorted by the state protection service, and judge anna korwin piotrowska announced she was taking over leadership; president nawrocki cut short a trip to senegal. in a november 4 euobserver op ed, law professor alberto alemanno argues the operation aimed to restore a lawful court rather than capture it, citing the eu court of justice's 2025 ruling that the tribunal is not independent and a may 2026 european court of human rights order, but says it raises legitimate questions of method. the same day the international commission of jurists said the takeover contravenes international standards on judicial independence. a deputy prime minister has since floated a 'constitutional reset'. hoax bomb threats jump from airliners to tv newsrooms, signed 'mikhail andropov', with a russian manosphere name attached on november 6 ireland's rté, britain's sky and bulgaria's nova tv received emails under the subject 'message to the west' claiming a bomb would go off in 45 minutes; nothing was found, but rté ran music and recorded messages for three hours and nova evacuated its newsroom. the sender, signing with a name echoing soviet leader yuri andropov, claimed responsibility for the previous week's airline threats (at least seven flights on november 3 and twelve on november 5). ansa reported the threats were sent in the name of 'fighters of men's state', a reference to a russian misogynist movement; its founder vladislav pozdnyakov denies any role and says the group has not existed since 2021. european authorities have not attributed the campaign. finland runs two tracks: its president calls putin while its prime minister calls a total ban on russians a logical next step prime minister petteri orpo announced the foreign ministry is preparing new entry restrictions on russian citizens, including athletes, ahead of two nhl games in helsinki next week, the finlandia trophy skating event on november 20 and 21, and a ski world cup in ruka on november 27 to 29. he described a complete ban on russians entering finland as a logical next step. the move follows an october court of arbitration for sport ruling reinstating russia's hockey team, which federations in sweden, finland, latvia, norway, denmark and czechia say they will refuse to play. it comes days after president alexander stubb and norway's jonas gahr støre phoned putin. who speaks for europe? støre defends talking to putin, frederiksen is 'very skeptical', eu leaders decide november 13 us, ukrainian, nato and european officials met in brussels on november 5 on guarantees for kyiv and a wider european security framework. norway's støre argued putin should hear europeans directly rather than through trump's envoys, while danish prime minister mette frederiksen said she doubts russia wants peace with ukraine or europe. peskov said europe has sent no proposals and cannot decide who represents it; france's barrot said on november 8 that europe will take part in abu dhabi, and eu leaders meet november 13 on representation. serbia's winning student list calls kosovo 'temporarily occupied' and russia a 'traditional partner' two weeks after the october 25 election, serbia still has no government; rté reports the student list took about 53 percent and 140 of 250 seats, with cardiologist ilija srdanović, former central bank governor dejan šoškić and former basketball player dejan bodiroga floated for prime minister. in a november 7 column, former uk europe minister denis macshane notes that movement founder radomir saičić called kosovo temporarily occupied territory days before the vote, that its website calls kosovo's government 'provisional institutions', and that its program names russia a traditional partner on open questions including kosovo. srdanović says the movement is committed to eu integration and will respect agreements signed by earlier governments, without confirming the 2013 brussels agreement. taiwan detains the founder of the tiny taiwan people's communist party over alleged beijing money in neighborhood chief races prosecutors in tainan and hsinchu searched premises on november 7 and announced on november 8 that lin te-wang, who founded the taiwan people's communist party in 2017, is in detention without outside contact. they allege he took funding and instructions from the chinese communist party to run for ward (li) chief in tainan's xinying district and to bankroll a party colleague, chen zhen-zhou, in a hsinchu ward race. investigators say the pair recruited voters for all expenses paid trips to china, possibly as vote buying; 13 suspects were questioned in tainan. chen was freed on nt$50,000 bail and prosecutors plan to appeal. taiwan counts 131 people targeted by chinese transnational repression and moves to write the offense into law mainland affairs council deputy minister liang wen-chieh told a legislative committee on november 5 that 131 taiwanese were targeted in 149 incidents between 2005 and 2026, through nine methods ranging from physical attacks and criminal prosecution to border bans, sanctions and digital harassment. he cited assaults on japanese commentator akio yaita and taiwanese comedian huang yi-hao as suspected ccp linked cases. justice minister cheng ming-chien said current law falls short: nothing bans reporting taiwanese to china's online informant portal, and the stalking law does not cover politically motivated following. the justice ministry is drafting anti-infiltration act amendments to define transnational repression and add asset confiscation. taiwan shuts its papua new guinea office and cuts off lng spot buying; washington voices concern taiwan's foreign ministry said on november 6 it will close its representative office in papua new guinea and withdraw all staff after port moresby renewed a demand, first made in july, that the office go. taipei is also ending technical and medical missions and scholarships and has stopped spot purchases of png liquefied natural gas; it says its buying equals about a third of png's exports and that it had planned roughly 500,000 tonnes in the first half of 2026. the ministry blamed chinese political and economic pressure, though the report offers no evidence on png's own reasoning. the us expressed concern about the forced closure on november 8. beijing writes its reading of un resolution 2758 into a joint statement with gabon; taipei protests after talks between xi jinping and gabonese president brice clotaire oligui nguema, china's foreign ministry released a joint statement on november 6 in which gabon reaffirmed the one china principle. taiwan's foreign ministry said on november 7 that the text distorted un general assembly resolution 2758 of 1971, which addresses china's un seat and does not mention taiwan. taipei accused beijing of routinely using bilateral meetings to get partners to sign language that undermines the republic of china's sovereignty. joshua wong gets 10 more years for foreign collusion, weeks before he was due out hong kong high court judge tam yiu-ho sentenced activist joshua wong on november 5 to 10 years for conspiring with foreign forces under the 2020 national security law, starting from 13 years and discounting for his september guilty plea. the case covers july to november 2020, when prosecutors say he worked with exiled activist nathan law to seek foreign sanctions. wong had been due for release in january from his subversion sentence; he will now be about 40 on release around 2036. police national security chief steve li urged nathan law to return and surrender; us rep. john moolenaar and taiwan's mainland affairs council called for his release. beijing's spy agency turns japan's corporate data breach wave into a public lesson china's ministry of state security said on november 8 that more than 115 million records were reportedly compromised in japan in six weeks from september to mid october, including over 22 million customer records from one unnamed software company and millions of restaurant membership records. it argued that such everyday data lets foreign intelligence services profile and target people, and blamed over collection, slow patching, weak access controls and outsourced suppliers. it named no companies and the figures are unverified. new zealand election: labour wins the most votes, national wins the most seats, and the government survives by one seat on preliminary counts electoral commission preliminary results for the november 7 vote give labour 29.36 percent (710,330 votes) and national 29.21 percent (706,680), but national takes 42 seats to labour's 36 because it won 42 electorates, producing an enlarged 131 seat parliament where 66 is a majority. the governing national, act and nz first bloc has 67 seats; labour, greens and te pāti māori have 57, or 64 with the new opportunity party's 7. about 399,365 special votes (roughly 14 percent of the total) are uncounted and official results are due november 27, with the government in caretaker mode until then. turnout was an estimated 74.6 percent, down from 78.2 percent in 2023. new zealand's overhang turns a vote splitting campaign and a new party into the story; senior national ministers fall out rnz's election coverage on november 8 debated whether the overhang was artificially created by harry mowbray's split your vote campaign, which urged voters to give electorate votes and party votes to different parties, while another analysis argued the campaign did not explain national winning two of three general electorates. because national won more electorates than its party vote entitles it to, list mps including deputy leader and finance minister nicola willis and speaker gerry brownlee miss out on preliminary numbers, and chris bishop lost hutt south to labour. luxon said he would build a relationship with opportunity and call its leader qiulae wong; before the vote wong said opportunity would talk first to the party with most seats and would not back a government with winston peters as foreign minister. north korea's munitions chief speaks for the nuclear program, then the military fires several missile types at once on november 2 kim jeong-sik, first vice director of the workers' party munitions industry department, condemned iron mace, a closed south korea and us tabletop drill on integrating us nuclear forces with seoul's conventional forces, as proof washington plans a nuclear attack. seoul's unification ministry called it unusual for a munitions official to issue such a statement. on november 4 the north fired several missiles from the sondok area, and kcna said it tested a new air defense missile and ran a fire strike drill. stars and stripes notes the fbi blames pyongyang for stealing over $6 billion in crypto from binance, which the north denies, and that the us, eu and australia added sanctions last week. malaysia: umno pays najib's rm50 million fine and he goes home under house arrest, splitting the unity government umno's secretary general confirmed the party paid former prime minister najib razak's rm50 million fine, and the high court ordered house arrest once it was settled; najib left kajang prison and his residence was declared a prison. prime minister anwar ibrahim said he disagreed with umno paying but called it the party's decision, while the attorney general's chambers sought to put the house arrest on hold and dap leader anthony loke said his resignation would take effect when najib got home. sarawak's state election is set for december 12. the hormuz war shows up in southeast asian prices: thai inflation breaches target, philippine inflation at a three year high thai inflation rose to 3.9 percent, breaching the bank of thailand's target for the first time in over three years, and philippine inflation hit a three year high, according to regional headlines on november 6. indonesia meanwhile reported faster third quarter growth and forecast 5.4 percent for 2026, and analysts expect bank negara malaysia to raise rates by 25 basis points in 2027. myanmar's junta sets april 4, 2027 by elections to extend its parliament into contested areas; tokyo keeps it on a blacklist myanmar authorities announced by elections for april 4, 2027, framed as expanding parliament's reach, and said they were confident of holding territory. tokyo rejected a myanmar request to be removed from a blacklist, laos and myanmar agreed to tighten border security, and bangladesh reported rescuing rohingya refugees during a gun battle on the border. philippines: beijing accuses philippine politicians of intolerable conduct as manila counts on the new democratic congress for military aid china accused philippine politicians of conduct it called intolerable as tensions rose, while a philippine envoy said the incoming democratic led us congress will sustain military aid, according to november 6 regional headlines. rappler's maritime disputes page carries reports on taiwan calling a chinese trawler seizure psychological warfare and experts seeking to price environmental damage in the west philippine sea, but its items are undated. unodc puts afghan opium at nearly 1,500 tonnes in 2026, about five times last year, as doha process drug talks open in termez afghanistan international reported that the un office on drugs and crime estimated 2026 afghan opium production at nearly 1,500 tonnes, up from about 300 tonnes in 2025; the taliban interior ministry rejected the report. a counter narcotics working group of the doha process, the un led track for engaging the taliban, opened a two day meeting in termez, uzbekistan, on november 5. the same outlet reported the eu saying it has not recognized the taliban and has put five individuals on its human rights sanctions list. pakistan arrests an afghan taliban member in focused on war coverage, wrote that trump might renew strikes on iran around the new moon because the military prefers darkness. he says outright he does not know, and argues a weakened trump may want a dramatic legacy act while the democratic congressional leadership will not change policy much. moon of alabama: stephen miller's promotion protects defense secretary hegseth moon of alabama argues that naming stephen miller white house chief of staff shields pete hegseth from being made the scapegoat for the iran war and the midterm loss. the post leans on a new york times account of miller's role, hegseth's public congratulations and reporting on the two men's close social ties. georgia's secretary of state finds an uncounted memory card that flips a state house seat to the republican a routine check after the election found about 388 more voters checked in than ballots reported in seminole county, part of southwest georgia's house district 154. counting the missed election day memory card turned democrat harry james' 58 vote lead into a 262 vote lead for republican gerald greene. secretary of state brad raffensperger called the failure unacceptable and opened an investigation; zerohedge relayed the ajc, wctv and the current. city journal sting: an la immigrant rights group hosted an official voting center while staff recommended candidates christopher rufo and two colleagues report that chirla, a los angeles immigrant rights nonprofit that has received over $100 million in california funds since 2019, hosted an official county voting center during a get out the vote event where an employee walked them through which candidates to pick. they argue this may break california's 100 foot electioneering rule and federal limits on 501(c)(3) charities, and urge the irs and treasury to act. zerohedge republished the piece. kunstler on zerohedge: the midterms were a fraud built to launch a 'color revolution' novelist and blogger james howard kunstler claims democrats registered ineligible and fictitious voters to flood the count with mail ballots, then plan riots and a push to declare trump illegitimate, possibly leading to the insurrection act. he says a doj voter roll audit will expose it, and alleges minnesota fraud involving peggy flanagan and tim walz. epoch times: trump backs nvidia's jensen huang despite a probe into his affair with an alleged chinese spy the epoch times, a paper founded by falun gong followers and hostile to beijing, reports that nvidia's board opened a probe into whether ceo jensen huang was targeted by chinese wrongdoing and floated bringing him on next week's china trip. rubio called it an internal corporate matter. war room: bannon says 'caravans' are already moving after the democratic win on war room, times that iran had no bomb program on judge andrew napolitano's libertarian show judging freedom, former cia officer john kiriakou said three separate national intelligence estimates before the war concluded iran had no nuclear weapons program, and that analysts judged the war a mistake. he also cited a leaked cia 'red cell' paper suggesting israel, not iran, could break apart. zerohedge carried the segment, which also featured former analyst larry johnson. the midterms were stolen by fraud, possibly through hacked tabulators, as the opening move of a democratic 'color revolution' (new hooks since nov 7: a michigan tabulator wifi claim and a real georgia memory card error) a new migrant caravan was organized and timed to the democratic midterm win, possibly funded by moneyed interests protecting him for the china trip the israel lobby is going underground, moving money into shell pacs to secretly split progressive votes no new confirmed tanker strike for november 7 to 8 surfaced in briefs.title: Paraguay Ousts Its President, Sudan Accuses Ethiopia, Iran Faces a Winter Gas Crisis
briefs.bluf: This edition was rebuilt around what most outlets missed. Paraguay's Senate removed President Santiago Peña 44 to 0 after a bank collapse froze deposits for nearly half the country, putting one of Taiwan's last allies in flux. Sudan formally accused Ethiopia at the UN of hosting RSF drone launches, as Ethiopia's own war reignites on three fronts and an Ebola outbreak in Congo passes 10,700 cases with spread to Kenya and Nigeria. In the Gulf, Iran faces a winter gas shortfall and is executing protesters while it negotiates, the Houthis are licensing Red Sea shipping by email, and Gulf fertilizer and sulphur exports are down about 70%, a food and metals shock that will hit after the oil headlines fade. In Washington, Stephen Miller becomes chief of staff Monday and a judge threw out the DOJ suit against Alaska's Senate certification.
briefs._s: paraguay ousts its president, sudan accuses ethiopia, iran faces a winter gas crisis this edition was rebuilt around what most outlets missed. paraguay's senate removed president santiago peña 44 to 0 after a bank collapse froze deposits for nearly half the country, putting one of taiwan's last allies in flux. sudan formally accused ethiopia at the un of hosting rsf drone launches, as ethiopia's own war reignites on three fronts and an ebola outbreak in congo passes 10,700 cases with spread to kenya and nigeria. in the gulf, iran faces a winter gas shortfall and is executing protesters while it negotiates, the houthis are licensing red sea shipping by email, and gulf fertilizer and sulphur exports are down about 70%, a food and metals shock that will hit after the oil headlines fade. in washington, stephen miller becomes chief of staff monday and a judge threw out the doj suit against alaska's senate certification. stephen miller becomes white house chief of staff after the midterm loss trump named stephen miller chief of staff starting november 9, replacing susie wiles. trump frames it as wiles moving to his political operation; zerohedge highlights a claim on joe rogan's show that her office signed off on nearly every major decision. judge throws out doj suit to hold up alaska's senate certification judge sharon gleason ruled doj lacked standing in united states v. alaska. doj wanted ballots set aside while it checked whether votes for a second 'daniel j. sullivan' were meant for sen. dan sullivan. she found ballots already mixed and impossible to separate without breaking ballot secrecy. doj reportedly opens a grand jury probe into the dobbs leak the dc us attorney's office under jeanine pirro is reportedly subpoenaing people who worked at the supreme court in 2022. the court's own 2023 inquiry never found the leaker. the report builds on a november 5 new york times story with anonymous sources. a 181 page progressive memo tells democrats to subpoena ceos, not just the white house the groundwork collaborative wants hearings with landlords on junk fees, sports betting apps on addiction, grocers on surveillance pricing and ai firms. rep. greg casar wants ai ceos first; the centrist progressive policy institute is pushing back. wealth taxes lose in california but move forward in washington and colorado california's one time 5% billionaire tax was trailing about 56 to 44, and a measure banning such taxes was winning. repeal of washington's 9.9% tax on income over $1 million was failing; a colorado millionaire surtax was narrowly ahead. voters rejected data centers in 38 of 40 plus local races six cities banned data centers outright and 12 capped their power draw. mayors who backed hyperscale projects lost in yukon, oklahoma (a recall) and burgin, kentucky. dc's socialist mayor elect walks into a federal collision janeese lewis george will run a city where congress can veto laws and approve the budget, the national guard is deployed and there is a $1.1 billion gap. the aclu of dc wants a local law letting residents sue federal officers who violate their rights. iran hangs two isfahan protesters; two more death sentences in mashhad amirhossein maleki and amirhossein ebrahimi, sentenced over the january protests, were hanged. a single source told iran international that maleki went through a staged hanging after retracting his confession. iran human rights counts at least 36 protesters executed since march. gas rich iran faces a winter shortage and leans on russia the national gas company says about 130 million cubic meters a day, roughly 16% of last year's output, is still offline after the march strikes. about 11 provinces could face shortages. hardliners float leaving the nuclear treaty; the atomic chief attacks the iaea head after the us midterms, hardline commentators say a democratic congress changes nothing and propose threatening to leave the npt; hamshahri printed a map of us bases in europe. atomic energy chief mohammad eslami called iaea head rafael grossi an agent of iran's enemies. kurdish government splits: puk quits after kdp seats a speaker without it kurdistan's parliament met for the first time in almost two years and elected kdp's vala farid speaker with the puk boycotting. puk leader bafel talabani says if the kdp appoints regional leaders alone, the puk will appoint its own in sulaymaniyah. us reportedly threatens to label iraq a state sponsor of terrorism over militia weapons unnamed sources say the us chargé told baghdad it could face sanctions and the label without a concrete plan to bring militia weapons under state control by june 30, 2027. the militias' conditions include us and turkish troops leaving and the kurdish peshmerga being dissolved. the houthis are issuing red sea transit permits by email since declaring a blockade of saudi arabia, the houthis have answered ships' emailed requests for safe passage, usually within 24 hours, per a wsj investigation. one chinese container ship got a seven day permit and an offer of houthi alerts. aramco profit up 34.6% as it plans a bigger hormuz bypass pipeline aramco's third quarter net profit rose to $36.2 billion, and the ceo said engineering has begun to expand the east west pipeline to the red sea from 7 to 10 million barrels a day. saudi arabia signs a defense pact and $403 million in deals with syria after ahmed al sharaa's second riyadh trip in a month, the saudis funded health centers, 10,000 home repairs, water systems and aleppo's power plant, and the defense ministries signed a cooperation agreement. documents tie press tv's london office to the sovereign media network correspondence shows press tv london paid ahmed kaballo about £41,700, partly in cash via the embassy. kaballo founded african stream, which the state department says rt secretly ran, and now leads sovereign, which reuses press tv content and contributors. hebron siege lifted after election week as october set a record for settler attacks the army withdrew from hebron on november 2 after a closure that displaced about 5,000 people; the governor puts losses at 10 to 12 million shekels a day in a city that makes about 40% of palestinian industrial output. ocha counted 397 damaging settler attacks in 26 days of october, the most since 2006. egypt's army uses armed drones on gold miners at the sudan border, arrests 691 the army says it arrested 151 egyptians and 540 foreigners and confirmed using armed drones; a rights group blames an october air strike on a border mine that killed at least 72 miners. the kyiv 'torture house' clash: part real grievance, part influence op about 200 people stormed a national guard transit house near kyiv holding mobilized men and deserters; officers used tear gas and warning shots. the woman who set it off posing as a medic was a cosmetologist and has been detained. ukraine's anticorruption bureau closes the midas probe; an sbu official threatened a gun during searches nabu finished its investigation into the mindich energy kickback scheme, alleging 10 to 15% skimmed from energoatom contracts and over $111 million laundered. in another case nabu says a senior sbu official obstructed searches and threatened to use a firearm; sbu special forces showed up and the acting sbu chief fired two officials. putin ratifies a deal letting bailiffs pull bank data on russians abroad russian bailiffs can now ask kazakhstan, belarus, azerbaijan, kyrgyzstan, tajikistan and uzbekistan where a debtor lives, works and banks, without notifying them. drone force recruiters found at 49 of russia's top 50 universities novaya gazeta europe and molniya found recruiting at 228 universities in 79 regions; students with poor grades face shortened retake deadlines and threats of expulsion followed by conscription. st petersburg cuts its army sign up bonus nearly ninefold the city cut its bonus from 3.5 million rubles to 400,000, its second cut in two weeks; mari el and mordovia did the same, and the defense ministry proposed pushing december pay into january. inside kiriyenko's propagandist training pipeline the 'new media workshop', run through sanctioned dialog regiony and linked to the doppelgänger operation, claims 1,700 graduates staffing rt, solovyov live and outlets in occupied ukraine. kremlin source: putin saw the finnish and norwegian call as an opening to europe per farida rustamova's vlast newsletter, putin views finland and norway as softer than berlin, paris and london; both want a standing channel, and kyiv coordinated the october 26 call. armenia's opposition unites after billionaire karapetyan's arrest the russian armenian billionaire and 35 associates were jailed; hours later opposition groups formed an alliance against constitutional changes baku demands before signing the peace treaty. georgia's ruling party moves to limit election challenges; russia bans a pro european party watchdogs warn a georgian dream bill limits challenges to final results to technical errors and scraps random recounts. the same day russia declared the opposition party droa undesirable. us licenses hungary's mol to start taking serbia's nis refinery from russia ofac allowed mol initial steps, transfer of russian origin securities and russian approvals, but not closing; budapest expects a deal by december 11. china's top military command is down to two men after the plenum purge after the fifth plenum expelled 33 members, 16 of them military, only xi jinping and zhang shengmin hold seats on the seven seat central military commission. the plenum also told provincial bosses to speak last in meetings and curbed demands for personal loyalty; retired general wang ning was removed from the top advisory body november 5. beijing passes a cross border anticorruption law with global reach the npc standing committee passed a law giving beijing new tools to chase offshore assets; earlier drafts also aimed to counter foreign corruption probes of chinese firms. a wuhan court is hearing a $53.5 billion covid 'defamation' suit against missouri chinese authorities and research institutes sued the us state of missouri over covid claims, and hearings began. china's central bank brakes the yuan with its first fx reserve hike in five years banks' foreign currency reserve requirement rises from 4% to 6% on november 15, locking up an estimated $20 to 25 billion. the yuan had risen 14 sessions straight; it then fell to a two week low. new zealand votes today with a 6% party holding the balance the final 1news verian poll had national 30, labour 29, greens 16, act 10, nz first 8 and the opportunity party 6.2, leaving both blocs short of 61 seats. unemployment hit 5.7%, an 11 year high. indonesia busts a ring trafficking its citizens into russia's army police arrested 13 suspects, including two russians and a ukrainian, with 58 alleged victims recruited through tiktok and facebook ads and sent on tourist visas. jakarta formally asked moscow to stop recruiting indonesians. north korea rehearses knocking out allied airbases, with doctored photos kcna reported anti aircraft missile tests and a cruise missile dropping cluster munitions on a mock runway; nk news found the images heavily manipulated. border loudspeakers are installed but silent. pyongyang's quiet diplomatic thaw before apec kim jong un's international department chief went to beijing ten days after kim visited dandong; brazil's first ambassador in a decade took up his post. kim yo jong said talks with the us are possible but not necessary and rejected the fbi's attribution of the $6.3 billion binance theft. thailand triples tax on imported evs as chinese competition bites the cabinet raised excise on imported battery evs from 10% to 35% starting january to protect local manufacturing. pakistan's ousted provincial chief is still missing as the coalition cracks since emergency rule in khyber pakhtunkhwa on october 11, former chief minister sohail afridi and two pti lawmakers are in 'protective custody' and 200 plus public order cases were filed. coalition partner bilawal bhutto told the government to stop fighting everyone; jui-f protested alleged drone surveillance of fazlur rehman's home. havana reportedly met us officials in new york the day its foreign minister denied talks martí noticias, citing anonymous sources, reports vice minister carlos fernández de cossío led an unannounced meeting with us officials during the un general assembly on september 24, the same day bruno rodríguez told ap no meetings were planned. barbados pm: cuba needs food and power before talk of political change mia mottley told cnn cuba must first secure food and energy, and this time did not blame the embargo. paraguay's senate removes president santiago peña, who is detained at home the senate voted 44 to 0 to remove peña for poor performance after the central bank took over ueno bank, freezing deposits for about 3 million clients, close to half the country. prosecutors accuse him of favoring a bank he had business ties to, including with public pension money. vice president pedro alliana serves until 2028. venezuela bombs an eln camp, breaking 20 years of chavista tolerance government drones hit an eln guerrilla camp in apure, apparently with a cocaine lab, killing at least 19; the nyt reported us help. machado and gonzález back a us plan: new courts first, elections within six months the state department plan would name new supreme court and electoral council members by year end, declare the presidency vacant, then hold a vote within six months, possibly july 24. venezuela's reserves fall despite $90 oil oikos research finds prices up 245% since december while the bolívar fell 198%, and the central bank lost a net $608 million in reserves; the budget assumed $55 oil. venezuela softens its hate law: prison out, dollar fines in a first reading replaces 10 to 20 year sentences with fines of 500 to 10,000 times the dollar rate; press unions want repeal and 140 web domains stay blocked. nicaragua drops cuban and venezuelan troops from its 2027 military permits but keeps russia decree 13/2026 lists foreign forces allowed in for exercises; for the first time since 2020 cuba and venezuela are out, russia keeps the largest quota. bukele's 2,000 troops in haiti operate outside the un force about 2,000 salvadoran soldiers with armor and air support deployed after an october ambush; the un says most sit outside the gang suppression force. a gang boss wrote to the un seeking a truce. colombia's forensic institute pushes back on soldiers moving bodies after combat medicina legal asked that troops be barred from moving bodies or belongings on their own under a draft decree on deaths in security operations. mexico's election authority files a criminal complaint after its chair quits the ine asked prosecutors to investigate former chair guadalupe taddei, who resigned over ties to a contractor; about 30 senior staff have left and all contracts, including voter id production, are under review. the ai fake id kingpin is free and explains how he beat bank checks yuriy nazarenko's onlyfake sold more than 10,000 ai generated ids at about $15 each, used by north korean fake it workers; he pleaded guilty, served about a year and left the us. ice moving to deport up to 80 afghans, including people who aided us forces the free press profiles a former kabul police officer who worked with us troops, now held in louisiana; 66 democratic lawmakers asked rubio to cancel the flights, reportedly routed through pakistan. sudan takes ethiopia to the un security council over rsf drones launched from ethiopian soil khartoum cites 70 attacks with 187 one way drones from february to october, 28 in october alone, killing 176 soldiers; it names asosa airport, the kurmuk border area and bahir dar airbase as launch sites. addis says sudan's army backs tplf linked rebels. ethiopia's old enemies now fight together: fano cuts the a2 highway amhara fano fighters reportedly took ibnat and cut parts of the a2 between dessie and woldia, addis ababa's supply line north, while federal forces push toward sheraro in tigray. tplf and fano leaders released a joint video vowing to overthrow the government. fighting over moyale pushes about 50,000 people into kenya; grenades hit a kenyan school ethiopian somalis and oromos have fought over moyale since october 18; on november 1 three rpgs fired from ethiopia hit a primary school in kenyan moyale. somalia's supreme court strikes down the president's term extension a day after he fired the chief justice the court ruled hassan sheikh mohamud's one year extension unlawful and that his term ended in may; he had dismissed chief justice bashe yusuf ahmed the night before. uganda will pull all its troops out at the end of next year. nigerian court voids atiku's opposition nomination ten weeks before the vote the federal high court threw out the adc leadership under david mark, and atiku abubakar's nomination fell with it; the adc will appeal and blames the ruling apc, which denies a role. guinea expels more than 8,000 burkinabè gold miners expulsions followed a ban on artisanal mining in northeast guinea; burkina's security minister says miners were injured and killed and ouagadougou got no notice. tanzania acquits tundu lissu of treason but jails him four years for incitement the opposition leader, held 19 months, was cleared of the capital charge and convicted of a lesser one he was never charged with. bundibugyo ebola passes 10,700 confirmed cases, with spread to kenya and nigeria as of november 4, drc had 10,741 confirmed cases and 5,230 deaths across eight provinces, worst in ituri. kenya has nine cases; a nigeria case was flown to switzerland. no licensed vaccine exists for this strain; a trial began in bunia october 23. guinea bissau cancels a us funded hepatitis b trial that withheld vaccine from newborns the study would have enrolled 14,000 newborns, half without the birth dose who recommends; police seized vaccines from the research center. trump's epstein letter suit against the wsj dismissed for good judge darrin gayles in miami dismissed the defamation suit with prejudice because trump again failed to plead actual malice; trump plans to appeal. gulf fertilizer and sulphur exports down about 70% see analysis you wouldn't think of: the food and battery metals shock lands after the oil headlines fade. judge lets florida's terrorist label on cair stand; the group shuts down in the state judge allen winsor denied cair's bid to block its designation under hb 1471; cair says it must stop advocacy in florida and will appeal. he did bar punishing cair staff or lawyers. appeals court: florida's medicaid cutoff notices violated due process an 11th circuit panel led by trump appointee barbara lagoa upheld an order requiring florida to explain the income and household figures it used to end coverage for nearly 500,000 people. fort myers ousts its mayor; lee school board chair loses city employee amber ware unseated mayor kevin anderson, and crystal johnson beat lee school board chair armor persons. florida's amendment 3 passed with about 62%; state economists project a $45.8 billion five year hit to local governments. vips memo: 'iran is not bluffing' veteran intelligence professionals for sanity, including ray mcgovern, larry johnson and scott ritter, tell trump iran expects a new us attack and may strike first, warn of a possible israeli false flag, and propose iran shipping out its enriched uranium under inspection. antiwar.com: ending israel aid is cosmetic, support moves into the pentagon budget dave decamp argues trump's pledge to end israel's yearly aid by end of 2026 hides deeper integration via the defense bill. scott ritter: europe's nuclear umbrella now runs through paris ritter argues macron's forward deterrence spreads french nuclear forces across europe while paris alone sets the stakes, with finland joining. craig murray calls poland's constitutional tribunal crisis an attempted coup the former uk diplomat says the october 30 move on poland's constitutional tribunal, backed by the tusk government and riot police, was a coup, and that western media leave out the ukraine angle. jonathan cook: a new uk 'hierarchy of racism' in schools cook says the bell review of antisemitism in schools, adopted in full, ranks antisemitism above other racisms and chills palestine solidarity in classrooms. zerohedge: the 'doomsday plane' flew east and nobody said why an e-4b nightwatch left offutt, crossed the midwest and turned south over northern virginia with no stated purpose; zerohedge ties it to a pentagon plan for bases to run 90 days off the grid. corbett report: synchronized emergency warnings around the world james corbett groups stockpiling advice from the uk, japan, germany, france, sweden, ireland and the eu with the pentagon's grid plan, and presents it as a fear campaign that may set up a false flag, cyberattack or financial collapse. zerohedge: iran is weathering the storm, saudi arabia is sinking brian mcglinchey argues mbs faces a risk of palace removal amid fiscal strain, stalled vision 2030 projects and houthi strikes. the defender: medical examiner emails discussed deaths after covid vaccination children's health defense reports foil emails from new york medical examiners discussing deaths after vaccination, which it says contradict public statements. midterm voting was rigged, including a houston fbi raid that found 20,000 fake democratic ballots and a deliberate scanner failure in westchester. governments are preparing people for a planned crisis: synchronized stockpiling advice, a pentagon grid survival plan and an unexplained doomsday plane flight. israel may stage a false flag to pull the us into a wider war with iran. medical examiners privately tracked covid vaccine deaths while officials said the shots were safe. foreign, possibly german, police were used in warsaw during the constitutional tribunal crisis. epoch times reports further minor us strikes on november 6 and an iranian claim of a downed mq-9; iran's gas output is still 16% below last year after the march strikes. abu dhabi talks open tuesday. indonesia busted a ring trafficking its citizens into russia's army. judge gleason dismissed the doj suit to delay alaska's certification. stephen miller replaces susie wiles as chief of staff on november 9. mississippi still uncalled. china's central military commission is down to xi and one vice chair after the plenum purge. paraguay, a taiwan ally, removed its president. report of an unannounced cuba and us meeting in new york in september; treasury sanctioned relatives of gaesa leaders. nothing new on attribution for the fridge attacks. briefs.title: Markets Turn on the AI Buildout, Iran Talks Stall on Sequencing, Two Senate Seats Still Open
briefs.bluf: The Iran war is still the defining factor. Three more tankers were damaged near Qatar on November 5, Trump said he may have to destroy the rest of the country, and a carrier group is heading to the region, while Qatar shuttles a plan that trades lifting the blockade and IAEA access for reopening Hormuz. Wall Street had its worst day in years: the Nasdaq fell 5.5% and the Nasdaq 100 6.4%, its worst session since March 2020, on fears that a Democratic Congress slows the AI buildout; futures point to a partial rebound this morning. Democrats hold 54 Senate seats with Mississippi (a margin of about 138 votes) and Alaska (ranked choice tally November 18) still open, and a Justice Department suit over a second Dan Sullivan on the Alaska ballot is the main certification risk. In Cuba, Yoani Sánchez was released after more than nine hours, but two other independent journalists remain jailed and the Law 186 government overhaul takes effect November 9. futures point to a partial rebound this morning. democrats hold 54 senate seats with mississippi (a margin of about 138 votes) and alaska (ranked choice tally november 18) still open, and a justice department suit over a second dan sullivan on the alaska ballot is the main certification risk. in cuba, yoani sánchez was released after more than nine hours, but two other independent journalists remain jailed and the law 186 government overhaul takes effect november 9. ukraine talks move to abu dhabi november 10 to 11 after a white house event marking the oleshky humanitarian truce. two senate races still open democrats hold 54 seats and flipped iowa, kansas, maine, ohio, north carolina, south carolina and texas. in mississippi, democrat scott colom leads sen. cindy hyde-smith 49.0% to 48.9% with about 3,600 mail ballots left; certification is due november 13. in alaska, mary peltola leads sen. dan sullivan 48.2% to 47.9% with ranked choice results due november 18. doj suit could stall alaska certification the justice department sued in october to block certification if peltola wins by less than the vote total of a second, unaffiliated candidate named daniel j. sullivan, arguing voters may have been confused. trump said he ordered the suit and has urged prosecuting peltola. legal scholars say the statute does not let doj enjoin a state certification. judge pauses the trump arch; la picks a new mayor a federal judge blocked construction of the planned arch for 14 days. in los angeles, nithya raman defeated mayor karen bass. in california, gov. newsom commuted 548 death sentences. more tankers hit; trump weighs a heavier strike the irgc said three more tankers were damaged november 5, two by mines and one by fire. ukmto reported a tanker hit by two projectiles 50 nautical miles north of madinat ash shamal, qatar. trump said he would rather not destroy the rest of the country but may have to, met his national security team, and spoke with the qatari emir, who urged restraint. a carrier group is heading to the region via singapore. diplomacy stuck on sequencing iran sent a nuclear proposal through qatar that it will discuss only after the us meets seven demands, including lifting sanctions and paying war reparations. a qatari draft reported by axios has the us lift the blockade and release some frozen funds and iran invite the iaea to bombed sites on day one, with hormuz reopening on day two and nuclear talks on the enriched uranium stockpile after that. iranian sources told reuters another us attack is more likely than a deal. tehran leans on the region foreign minister araghchi called his counterparts in the uae, qatar, saudi arabia, turkey, pakistan, oman and egypt. parliament speaker qalibaf mocked vice president vance as a losing gambler after vance blamed the war for the midterm losses. israel: herzog weighs who forms the next government after the october 27 election left netanyahu's bloc at 53 seats and gadi eisenkot's at 48, president herzog began consultations, meeting the smallest parties first. eisenkot was expected to have more endorsements than netanyahu. the election commission reviewed 9,069 polling stations and found no fraud. white house marks the oleshky truce melania trump hosted russian envoy kirill dmitriev and ukraine's david arakhamia to mark the six day humanitarian ceasefire in occupied oleshky (october 27 to november 1). more than 750 people were evacuated; russia refused to extend it. president trump met dmitriev but not the ukrainians and predicted a deal soon. abu dhabi talks next week witkoff and kushner lead the us side at three way talks in abu dhabi november 10 to 11. german chancellor merz hosts a coalition of the willing summit november 19. russia holds about 80% of donetsk. yoani sánchez released; two journalists still held yoani sánchez, director of 14ymedio, was released after more than nine hours in custody. adelth bonne gamboa of cubanet, arrested november 2, and henry constantín, jailed since september 16, remain detained. rsf, the inter american press association and amnesty international condemned the detentions. law 186 reshapes the government from november 9 the law, approved july 30 and published november 2 in the gaceta oficial, cuts the cabinet to 20 ministries plus the central bank and merges commerce, construction and agriculture into fewer bodies. officials present it as streamlining; critics see a shuffle that leaves the economic model untouched. protest count stays high the observatorio cubano de conflictos logged 542 protests and complaints in october and 85 repressive events. transition quiet no new annulment filings or street mobilization found. lula takes office january 1. pope leo begins south america tour the first us born pope is in uruguay november 6 to 8, argentina november 8 to 11 and peru november 11 to 17, about 50 events in 10 cities, including a return to chiclayo, where he was bishop, and a meeting with president milei. former fbi agent charged doj charged former fbi agent andrew reyes on november 5. details of the charges were not collected this cycle. election claims fade, alaska suit gives them a new hook rigging claims about the midterms have lost momentum as most losers conceded, but the doj suit over the second dan sullivan gives the "stolen seat" framing a new focus in alaska. fridge hacks: still no attribution no group has claimed or been named for the attacks on supermarket refrigeration controllers. belgium opened a prosecution and the eu called them deliberate. the danfoss and copeland flaws were disclosed by claroty august 9; forescout counted about 13,000 exposed systems. the pentagon is reviewing august freezer failures at military commissaries. mexican judge arrested in ryan wedding case a mexican judge was arrested over an alleged $2 million bribe tied to the case against ryan wedding, the former olympic snowboarder accused of running a cocaine network and ordering the killing of a federal witness. wedding was captured in mexico in january. doj launches super intelligence task force the department announced a task force on ai related crime the same day it charged a $129 million fraud marketed as a super intelligence investment. no new ofac actions found for november context: the cartel del noreste was designated october 13, venezuela's jorge rodríguez was delisted october 14, and foreign banks must exit panama's bicsa by november 14. deportations deepen school enrollment drops npr reports ice enforcement is accelerating enrollment declines in districts with large immigrant populations. doj also sued penn state over in state tuition for undocumented students. why the doomsday date keeps spreading writers revisiting the 1960 "doomsday" paper note that a specific date, a real scientific source and a friday the 13th make a claim shareable. the historian alan maceachern argues the lesson is about how confidently findings are presented. ai selloff after the election nvidia fell 9.2%, about $440 billion in value, and the largest tech stocks lost more than $1 trillion as investors priced in a congress that may slow data center and chip spending. south korea's kospi fell about 8 to 9% and halted trading. google: accept ai or lose search in schools from early 2027, gemini and search will be off by default on k-12 student accounts; schools that switch ai off entirely will also lose search. fairplay urged schools to consider other search engines. supreme court hears labor visa case november 10 department of labor v. sun valley orchards is argued monday. claim: a scientist said the world ends november 13 the date comes from a real 1960 science paper. its authors fitted a curve to population history that reached infinity in late 2026, and they picked friday the 13th partly as a joke. population growth peaked soon after and the curve stopped matching reality. hundreds leave oleshky more than 750 civilians left the occupied town during the six day truce, the largest humanitarian pause of the war in that area. the midterms were rigged through fake ballots and compromised machines democrats won by importing foreigners and registering them to vote (great replacement framing) ebola is a hoax, a western bioweapon, or a scheme for aid groups to make money a scientist predicted the world ends on friday, november 13, 2026 three more tankers damaged november 5 and ukmto reported a tanker hit by two projectiles 50 nautical miles north of madinat ash shamal, qatar. trump met his national security team and said iran would know soon enough; briefs.title: Baseline Edition: A Gulf War Under Domestic Pressure, a Hybrid Campaign in Europe, and Cuba Under Strain
briefs.bluf: The defining factor this week is the collision between the US war on Iran and US domestic politics: Democrats won both chambers on November 3 and the Vice President publicly blamed the war. Washington struck Iranian targets near Hormuz on the eve of the vote and tankers keep burning near the strait, while talks run through Gulf mediators. In Europe, a wave of hoax bomb threats against flights fits the pattern of a Russian linked hybrid campaign, unattributed so far. Russia killed 42 people at a Ukrainian aid center days before US mediated talks on November 10 and 11. Cuba is under severe strain from the oil blockade and is detaining independent journalists. This is the baseline edition, so status changes are measured from here.

jordan are running for minority leader; jeffries is running for speaker when congress convenes january 3. us strikes near hormuz on the eve of the midterms limited us strikes hit around qeshm, hengam and bandar abbas. iran's supreme national security council head said the strait stays closed until us addresses its conditions: lifting the naval blockade, waiving oil sanctions and a ceasefire including lebanon. more tankers on fire east of hormuz; tanker hit off qatar iranian state media reported two more tankers on fire. separately, the british military said a tanker was struck by projectiles off qatar. iran's security chief meets putin mohsen rezaei discussed regional issues in moscow, and iran says it will supply russian gas to neighboring countries. gaza and yemen at least four palestinians were killed in gaza on november 5. in yemen's taiz, government forces say they repelled a houthi attack; the un says water production has halved and hospitals are short of fuel. aid center strike toll reaches 42 russian bunker busting bombs hit a school used as an aid hub in komyshuvakha, then the shelter where people took cover. erdogan wants direct talks with putin; italy readies aid after talks with zelenskyy, erdogan said he wants to discuss ending the war with putin. italy is finalizing a new military aid package. putin seizes japan tobacco's russian operations; drone strike hits ozon warehouse moscow took control of jti's russian business. a drone strike set an ozon warehouse ablaze in southern russia. pla activity rebounds after typhoon lull 85 sorties from october 26 to november 1, 47 into the adiz. on november 3 to 4: 22 sorties, 7 pla navy ships and 5 official ships. beijing's ai enabled influence operations ahead of taiwan's local elections taiwanese officials report ai generated content and cyberattacks aimed at polarization and lower turnout before the november 28 vote. vietnam comments on china and laos military cooperation hanoi said the cooperation should contribute to regional stability. yoani sánchez detained in havana the 14ymedio founder was held about nine hours, the third detention of an independent journalist in havana this week after cubanet's camila acosta on tuesday. the us condemned the arrests. grid at about a third of demand the une forecast 958 mw available against 2,850 mw demand on november 2, with blackouts over 20 hours a day. government reorganization takes effect november 9 law 186 cuts central state agencies from 27 to 21. reported military mobilization cibercuba reports cuba mobilizing forces amid rising tensions with the us. transition settling after contested runoff lula won 51.8% to 48.2%. flávio bolsonaro's party acknowledged the result after his annulment call; trump called it rigged. colombia ends 'total peace' congress passed president de la espriella's bill: armed group members must disarm, identify fellow members, hand over recruited minors, surrender assets and reveal links to politicians to earn reduced sentences. leaders face at least 10 years. paraguay seizes bank tied to the president central bank took over ueno bank after its capital fell below half the legal minimum; about 3 million accounts and public pension funds frozen. poland arrests four over military supplies sent to russia part of a broader pattern of sabotage and procurement networks targeting the main aid route to ukraine. hoax bomb threats hit european aviation about ten flights threatened november 3 and four prague bound planes november 5. the eu transport chief says it is too early to say whether they are linked. prc influence operations target taiwan's november 28 vote officials cite ai generated content designed to polarize and depress turnout. narrative watch: iranian leadership messaging a statement attributed to mojtaba khamenei claims iran's control of hormuz shattered the myth of american invincibility. supermarket refrigeration systems hacked across europe unidentified hackers shut down supermarket fridges in several countries the same week as the flight threats; analysts see a pattern of low cost disruption. october ransomware roundup october incidents included a ransomware attack that disrupted patient care and surgeries at university of new mexico health sciences center. israel detains journalist abed abu shehadeh police and shin bet arrested the arab48 editor and +972 contributor in jaffa; a court extended his detention. rights groups call it part of a campaign against palestinian journalists. paraguay: ueno bank arrests prosecutors ordered the arrest of eight people including the bank's president and ceo. brazil: banco master case flávio bolsonaro is under investigation in the banco master case without formal charges, per mercopress. bangladesh garment workers win wage concessions after five days of protests and clashes with police, a new wage board agreed to a revised pay scale from december. workers seek about $242 a month. pakistan a federal judge in new york temporarily blocked the flights, which could have begun this week. advocates warn of taliban persecution of those who worked with us troops. rep. salazar: hispanic the security council failed to renew it. russia vetoed a us draft backing moroccan sovereignty; a rival russian draft also failed. south africa's anc heading for worst local result with 28% counted,
